title: ci(hook-selftests): discover the self-test matrices instead of enumerating them
body:
Fixes #6906

## What changed

`.github/workflows/hook-selftests.yml` names itself *"The standing caller for `.claude/hooks/*.selftest.sh`"* and was not one: its `steps:` were a hand-kept enumeration, so a new matrix shipped **uncalled** until someone remembered to edit this file. `guard-tree-enum.selftest.sh` is the receipt — it landed in both repos on the same card, objectstack's collector picked it up with no workflow edit, and here it had to be added by hand (the removed step even carries a comment saying so).

The three `run:` steps are replaced by one step that discovers its matrices:

```bash
mapfile -t selftests < <(find .claude/hooks -type f -name '*.selftest.sh' | sort)
```

Ported from objectstack's collector in its `lint.yml` (step *"Claude hook guard self-tests"*), keeping both load-bearing properties.

| file | why |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/hook-selftests.yml` | the change |
| `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` | paired write — this workflow's own section hand-listed two of the three matrices, and would otherwise describe the change incorrectly |
| `.changeset/6906-hook-selftests-collector.md` | empty-frontmatter changeset (CI-only; no published package's `src/` changed) |

`.claude/**` is **not** touched — governed surface, and this job is the runner, not the matrices. Verified mechanically against the base sha recorded at branch creation (`b458300ca`), not against a moving `origin/main`:

```
$ git diff --name-only b458300ca...HEAD | grep -c '^\.claude/'
0
$ node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test .github/workflows/hook-selftests.yml content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md .changeset/6906-hook-selftests-collector.md
NOT GOVERNED - 3 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.
```

## The two load-bearing properties, exercised rather than read

Both were exercised against the step's real `run:` block, extracted from the YAML by a parser (not retyped) and executed as GitHub executes it, under `bash -e`. Every negative case ran in a scratch directory; nothing under the repo's real `.claude/` was deleted, moved or disabled.

### 1. An empty discovery is RED

```
scratch dir with an EMPTY .claude/hooks/      -> exit 1
  "Hook self-tests - DISCOVERED NOTHING under .claude/hooks/."
scratch dir with NO .claude/ directory at all -> exit 1  (same message)
```

A step that verified nothing is not a pass: a renamed or moved directory cannot degrade this gate into a silent green no-op.

### 2. Tolerate-and-collect

Scratch `.claude/hooks/` with three stubs — `aaa-deliberately-red` (exit 1), `mmm-deliberately-red` (exit 3), `zzz-green` (exit 0, prints a marker):

```
-- .claude/hooks/aaa-deliberately-red.selftest.sh
FAIL  .claude/hooks/aaa-deliberately-red.selftest.sh
-- .claude/hooks/mmm-deliberately-red.selftest.sh
FAIL  .claude/hooks/mmm-deliberately-red.selftest.sh
-- .claude/hooks/zzz-green.selftest.sh
LATER-MATRIX-RAN - 7 passed, 0 failed
PASS  .claude/hooks/zzz-green.selftest.sh

Hook self-tests - the following FAILED:
  .claude/hooks/aaa-deliberately-red.selftest.sh
  .claude/hooks/mmm-deliberately-red.selftest.sh
                                                   -> exit 1
```

The later matrix still ran, both failures are named, and the step is still red.

**Counter-proof that the shape matters.** The same three stubs under a naive `for f in ...; do "$f"; done`:

```
exit 1, and "LATER-MATRIX-RAN" occurrences in the log: 0
```

`bash -e` aborts at the first red matrix and the rest are neither green nor red — which is exactly what this collector must not do. Please do not "simplify" the loop.

**`find`, not a flat glob.** A stub dropped at `.claude/hooks/nested/deep.selftest.sh` in the same scratch tree is discovered; `.claude/hooks/*.selftest.sh` would miss it.

## Coverage is not reduced — measured, not asserted

The hardcoded `run:` commands were parsed out of the workflow **as it exists on the base sha**, and set-differenced against what discovery returns on this tree:

```
hardcoded on b458300ca            discovered on HEAD
  guard-main-checkout-bash          guard-main-checkout-bash
  guard-shared-stash                guard-shared-stash
  guard-tree-enum                   guard-tree-enum

comm -23 hardcoded discovered  ->  0 lines   (nothing dropped)
comm -13 hardcoded discovered  ->  0 lines   (no net additions today)
```

Every self-test CI executes today is still executed. No self-test file was moved, renamed, skipped or quarantined.

## Every discovered self-test, run locally

Exit codes captured individually, before any pipe:

| self-test | exit | tail |
|---|---|---|
| `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.selftest.sh` | `0` | `121 passed, 0 failed` |
| `.claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.selftest.sh` | `0` | `41 passed, 0 failed` |
| `.claude/hooks/guard-tree-enum.selftest.sh` | `0` | `36 passed, 0 failed` |

And through the new collector, from the repo root: `exit 0`, `discovered 3 hook self-test(s)`, `Hook self-tests - all 3 ran and passed`. None was failing on `main`, so there is no finding to report there.

## `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` — read, unchanged

Its `OPTIONAL_CONTEXTS` entry for **Hook Self-Tests** is already count-free ("the PreToolUse guard self-test matrices must pass"), and its `paths` sentence is still accurate after this change. Nothing was edited there. The workflow header now records *why* it must stay count-free, next to the existing argument for count-free step names.

## Checks run (at `91eb09282`, the head of this branch)

| check | result |
|---|---|
| YAML parse of the workflow (PyYAML) + `bash -n` on the extracted `run:` block | parses; triggers, concurrency, permissions and `timeout-minutes` unchanged; syntax OK |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` | **90 files, 2572 tests passed** (includes `ci-cd-pipeline-doc`, `merge-queue-reporting`, `dependabot-merge-gate`, `lint-workflow`, the four `check-changeset-*` suites) |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | OK - 5820 tracked text files |
| `pnpm check:doc-fences` / `check:doc-types` / `check:doc-links` | OK |
| `pnpm check:shell-escape-residue` | OK - 205 files, 1320 fenced blocks |
| `pnpm check:skills-paths` | OK |
| `pnpm check:action-forward-parity` | OK |
| `pnpm check:governed-queue-guard` | OK - 132 self-test cases pass |
| `pnpm check:entry-guard` | OK |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | OK - 1 changeset added; no released source changed |

## Narrowings, declared

- **`pnpm check:doc-snippets` was NOT run to a verdict.** It exits 2, `PRECONDITION NOT MET` - it needs every package built, and its own output says that is "I could not run", not a failure. It reads TypeScript blocks in docs; this diff adds and removes **zero** fenced blocks (`git diff b458300ca...HEAD -- content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md | grep -c '^[+-].*\`\`\`'` is `0`), so there is nothing here it could judge. CI runs it either way.
- **Repo-wide `pnpm lint` was narrowed away, and the narrowing is measured, not assumed.** Population read from `eslint.config.js` itself: every `files:` selector in it is `.ts`/`.tsx`. This diff's `.ts`/`.tsx` count is `0` (3 changed files: one `.yml`, two `.md`), and it touches no `eslint.config.*` and no `tsconfig*`, so no untouched file's lint verdict can move either. CI runs the farm regardless.

Draft on purpose - the PM lands this. #6451 remains open and is a different mechanism (a missing self-test FILE); this PR is the runner that will call it once it exists.
